fixes.explanation: Jeremiah says God told him, “Buy for yourself the field with silver and call in witnesses…” (Jeremiah 32:25) Silver, plus people watching. Think of it as a signed receipt, with people there to say they saw it. Even with the city handed over, God's instructions on the field stayed the same.

God says, “Therefore I will remove it from My presence” (Jeremiah 32:31). It's serious. He says the city has aroused His wrath and fury from the day it was built until now. I think this one lands heavy, and we don't need to dress it up.

That isn't what God says here, baker. He says, “Therefore I will remove it from My presence” (Jeremiah 32:31). He also says, “Though I taught them again and again, they would not listen or respond to discipline.” (Jeremiah 32:33) What He announces here is removal, not another warning.

God says the opposite, baker. He includes the leaders too: “…they, their kings, their officials, their priests and prophets, the men of Judah, and the residents of Jerusalem.” (Jeremiah 32:32) Kings, priests and prophets are right there on the list. They aren't described as staying faithful.

That's right, friend. God lists kings and officials, priests and prophets, the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 32:32). The list is long on purpose, I think. It's a sober line, so we'll take it as it is.

God says, “They have turned their backs to Me and not their faces.” (Jeremiah 32:33) That's a picture anyone gets. Nobody has to explain what it means to be turned away from. He says He taught them again and again, and they would not listen.

God says it was “…something I never commanded them, nor had it ever entered My mind, that they should commit such an abomination and cause Judah to sin.” (Jeremiah 32:35) This is a heavy part, baker, about sons and daughters passing through the fire to Molech, a false god. I think this one hurts. God says it never came from Him.

God says, “…I will put My fear in their hearts, so that they will never turn away from Me.” (Jeremiah 32:40) Earlier God said they had turned their backs to Him and not their faces (Jeremiah 32:33). Here He promises that they will never turn away from Him. He's doing the heart work Himself.

God says it will happen “…because I will restore them from captivity, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 32:44) The reason is Him. He's the one who restores. Fields bought and deeds signed all over the land come from that promise.
